question: After four rounds, an internal newsletter item is accurate and well structured, but two headings use the wrong department names. The item is due in ten minutes. What should the editor do?
options: A) Rewrite her original request to include the department names, and produce a fresh version of the whole item.
B) Correct the two headings herself, since the remaining gap is smaller than the effort of another full round.
C) Publish the item as it stands and issue a short correction about the department names in next week's edition.
D) Run one more round asking for the department names to be corrected, and read the returned version closely.
correct_answers: B) Correct the two headings herself, since the remaining gap is smaller than the effort of another full round.
explanations: Regenerating the item risks the accuracy and structure that four rounds established, with ten minutes left to verify them.
Correct. Iteration is worth continuing while it is cheaper than doing the work by hand. Two headings are a few seconds of typing, so this is the point to stop iterating and finish it herself.
Publishing known errors and correcting them later costs the team credibility over a fix that takes moments.
Another round can fix two words, but it returns a whole document that has to be re-read to confirm nothing else moved.
